title: Comparative Cosmography Population Wave 001 — World Trees, Underworlds, Cosmic Mountains & Passage Systems
purpose: Add historically bounded comparative subjects that can populate the three-plane House without collapsing distinct religions into one cosmology.
epistemic_rule: Each tradition remains historically distinct. Plane and Tree placement are project navigation projections after own-tradition meaning, not claims of literal shared geography.

entries.source_summary: Yggdrasil is a central sacred tree whose roots and branches connect multiple realms; Eddic traditions place gods, wells, creatures and roots around it.
entries.structural_use: World-tree / axis comparator spanning roots, World and canopy.

entries.source_summary: The Duat is the Netherworld through which the sun god and deceased travel; Amduat traditions divide the nocturnal journey into hours and culminate in renewal/rebirth toward dawn.
entries.structural_use: Below-facing passage terrain and cyclical death/renewal route; strong example that underworld is not identical with punishment.

entries.source_summary: Sheol is the netherworld/realm of the dead, often dark and below, and is not simply equivalent to the later Christian notion of punitive Hell.
entries.structural_use: Below-facing death realm and provenance for later Hades/hell reception distinctions.

entries.tradition: Ancient Greek / later Jewish-Christian Greek reception
entries.source_summary: Hades is both a Greek underworld deity and name for the realm of the dead; in Greek biblical translation it often renders Sheol, while later traditions differentiate it from Gehenna/punishment.
entries.structural_use: Below-facing death realm plus reception-genealogy node.

entries.source_summary: Hel names both a ruler and realm of the dead in Norse tradition. Sources distinguish it from Valhalla and do not simply make it a universal place of punishment.
entries.structural_use: Below-facing realm/ruler pair; useful for separating death realm from moral punishment.

entries.source_summary: Valhalla is Odin's hall for selected slain warriors in Eddic tradition, distinct from Hel and embedded in a larger afterlife complex.
entries.structural_use: Heaven/World-facing hall/regime rather than generic heaven; useful for differentiated afterlife destinations.

entries.source_summary: Mount Meru/Sumeru functions as a central cosmic mountain in several South Asian cosmologies, with heavens/continents arranged around or above it in tradition-specific schemes.
entries.structural_use: High-value Mountain/axis comparator with cardinal/world-system organization.

entries.source_summary: The labyrinth is the winding structure of the Minotaur/Theseus cycle; ancient literary reception also associates the crane dance with imitating its winding path.
entries.structural_use: Route/threshold comparator for disorientation, hidden center, thread/return and successful exit rather than a new realm.

entries.source_summary: The caduceus is Hermes' herald staff and later depicted with intertwined serpents; Hermes is messenger and conductor of souls, making the object a mediation/peace/psychopomp symbol in classical reception.
entries.structural_use: Pillar/staff + messenger + crossing comparator; useful near Door/Axis but not identical to either.

research_boundaries: Do not equate Sheol, Hades, Hel, Duat or later Hell; their traditions and historical developments differ.
Do not treat Valhalla as a generic Norse Heaven or Hel as a generic punitive Hell.
Do not map Mount Meru, Yggdrasil or the Potato Axis as historically identical world centers.
Do not read labyrinth or caduceus symbolism as proof of a universal hidden esoteric system.
